title: Scaling GitHub for your Agents — Sam Morrow, GitHub
summary: GitHub's MCP server journey began publicly in April with the open-source local MCP server release, quickly becoming the most starred GitHub repo that week and attracting extensive community contributions. However, rapid feature additions caused tool proliferation exceeding 100 tools, degrading agent performance as context windows were consumed. LangChain's research confirmed that more tools create confused, forgetful agents. The team attempted mitigation through tool sets and dynamic tool selection, but these failed because most users never customized their JSON configurations, sticking with defaults. MCP spec proposals for tool grouping were repeatedly rejected. The team then optimized context by narrowing tools to general use cases, achieving approximately 49% reduction in initial context load, and grouping CRUD tools reduced defaults to about 40 tools. Output token optimization yielded 75%+ reduction for list pull requests. Tool reliability improved to over 95% success rate through intent-based design and server-side orchestration of multiple API calls. Security efforts addressed plain text, long-lived, over-privileged tokens by embracing OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, rejecting dynamic client registration due to operational concerns, and implementing automatic OAuth-scope-based tool filtering with step-up OAuth support. The server runs stateless with Redis session storage, creating a new SDK server instance per request with tools added dynamically based on configuration and policies. Sessions primarily identify self-reported client identity. An Insiders mode exposes experimental features like MCP apps with human-in-the-loop issue editing. Future directions include automatic server discovery, compositional tool use, and autonomous OAuth and tool selection, with thousands of tools becoming normal. The project has grown to over 11 million Docker downloads, 126 contributors, nearly 30,000 stars, almost 4,000 forks, and is fast approaching 8 million weekly tool calls.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Overview of GitHub's MCP public launch and community growth
sections.summary: Sam Morrow introduces GitHub's MCP server journey starting April last year with the open-source local MCP. It became the most starred repo that week, attracting high-volume public contributions that rapidly filled platform coverage gaps. After a month, agent performance degraded due to tool proliferation exceeding 100 tools and context window exhaustion.

sections.title: Challenges of tool proliferation and impact on agent context
sections.summary: LangChain research from February confirmed more tools create confused, forgetful agents. GitHub's expansive platform spans repos, issues, PRs, actions, and projects. The challenge was reducing tools without preventing diverse users from accessing individually needed tools.

sections.title: Mitigation via tool sets and dynamic discovery
sections.summary: Tool sets grouped related product tools for user selection. Dynamic tool selection let agents discover and enable tools in chunks. A RAG version for semantic tool search was built but unreleased. All solutions failed because users defaulted to standard settings and didn't configure JSON. MCP spec proposals for grouping were rejected multiple times. Read-only mode used by 17% maps to hint annotations but lacks client-side exposure.

sections.title: Optimizing API output tokens to improve efficiency
sections.summary: The team optimized usage patterns on the remote server, cutting initial context by 49% through focused general-case tools. Grouping CRUD tools reduced defaults to ~40 tools. Output token trimming for list pull requests achieved 75%+ reduction. Advanced approaches like code mode remain under experimentation.

sections.title: Improving reliability through intent-based tool design
sections.summary: Tool success rates reached 95%+. Some failures are unpreventable due to agent hallucination about write permissions. The team encoded agent intent into tool surfaces, orchestrating multiple API calls server-side to reduce round trips and improve success. Evals test tool descriptions against each other rather than micro-optimizing individually.

sections.title: Security strategy: OAuth 2.1 and PKCE implementation
sections.summary: Many users employ plain text, long-lived, over-privileged access tokens. GitHub embraced remote HTTP with OAuth 2.1 and added PKCE to their authorization server. Dynamic client registration was rejected due to unbounded app database growth, rate-limit bucketing challenges, and unreliable app identity. MCP's emerging client ID metadata approach may be supported.

sections.title: Managing prompt injection and security vulnerabilities
sections.summary: Invariant Labs published a prompt injection exfil attack targeting GitHub's MCP server. The vulnerability applies broadly to agent setups, not just GitHub MCP. Agent utility directly conflicts with security. Users span risk profiles from air-gapped Enterprise instances to full-token access. Simon Wilson's lethal trifecta blog post referenced.

sections.title: Using OAuth scopes for granular tool filtering
sections.summary: PAT tokens automatically filter tools by their scopes without user action. OAuth supports step-up challenges that interactively request scope approval, allowing tool calls to proceed rather than fail. VS Code integration leverages this with its existing GitHub token. Server tokens on actions lack user context, so user-specific tools are removed to eliminate constant failure sources.

sections.title: Stateless server architecture and Redis session management
sections.summary: The server runs completely stateless with Redis for session storage. A new SDK server instance is created on every request, with tools dynamically added based on configuration and policies. The server handles around 7 million tool calls weekly without session affinity. Sessions are primarily used to identify self-reported client identity for understanding which clients people use.

sections.title: Experimental features and human-in-the-loop UX
sections.summary: An Insiders mode exposes experimental feature flags to anyone who opts in. MCP apps, not yet generally released, enable human-in-the-loop editing of AI-generated issues, valuable for professional open source work where bot-generated content might be rejected. Morrow initially was unsure about the feature but came to love it for ensuring quality of posted content.

sections.title: Future outlook: Compositional tools and automation
sections.summary: Morrow predicts server discovery will become automatic and tool use will become compositional like bash piping, streaming data through tools. References Cloudflare's code mode, Anthropic's tool search API in Claude Code, and OpenAI's similar API. Expects thousands of tools to become normal, potentially reversing fewer-tools decisions. Users may not need to know what MCP is, with OAuth and tool selection becoming autonomous. Encourages experimentation with custom clients.

sections.title: Final project metrics: Downloads, forks, and volume
sections.summary: GitHub's MCP server has over 11 million Docker downloads of the stdio server, 126 contributors, over 2,300 issues and PRs at 7+ per day for over a year, nearly 30,000 stars, almost 4,000 forks, and is fast approaching 8 million weekly tool calls. Morrow acknowledges the intensity of the growth and encourages continued community engagement. A brief Q&A mentions MCP CLIs as a fun avenue for experimentation, particularly wrapping read-only tools in a CLI with proper help text.
